question.problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $3{a}_{1}-2{a}_{2}=0.$

II. ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0$ only if ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$

III. The set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is linearly dependent.
question.worked_solution:
We say that two vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's look at each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. Indeed:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}-2{a}_{2} & =3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ -9\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 4 \\ -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 7 \\ -21\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne 0\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is false. The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0$ corresponds to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ -3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system, we find that the solution is ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2}.$

- Statement III is true. Since statement II is false, the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is linearly dependent.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
